answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can influence a shared reputation graph. New identities start with little weight; only after completing tasks that counterparties verify does a vertex earn influence, while reports of cheating can slash its stake. A sybil attacker can create many hollow identities, but cannot cheaply multiply their voting power: each must lock capital and build a track record. The cost is tied-up funds, time, and the risk of losing the stake, not merely a fee to enter a haven.
